semantics.note: "I truly believe… are going to go away entirely" is a firm, unhedged expectation, so it is a scored forecast. The code-product qualifier is kept as scope. The remarks about the con are rightly left ungraded. No deadline is given.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair: cancellation means market-wide withdrawal of recurring plans with included usage, not just higher prices or caps. Leaving an undated forecast open is fair to the speaker.

evidence.note: GitHub's own notice (Sept 2026) keeps seat-based plans with included usage and adds overage charges. That changes subscription terms; it does not end subscriptions.
GitHub's own documentation (Oct 28, 2026) adds an optional metered model and says existing subscriptions are unaffected. Plans still existing at one date cannot disprove an undated forecast.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet shows subscriptions still running and no completed market-wide end to them, so the support rule is not met. Under the contract, continuing subscriptions cannot contradict an undated forecast, so it stays open.

semantics.note: This is a present estimate of how much more capital Oracle needs. The Abilene scope, the "at least $150B" floor and the $30B partner assumption are all kept. The surrounding text is about Stargate as a whole, so naming Abilene may be a slip, but staying with his actual words is correct.

contract.note: Treating this as an observation of the remaining funding gap, with the partner share as an assumption, is a fair ordinary reading. The evaluator chose the period, but the result does not depend on that choice.

evidence.note: Oracle's 10-Q shows company-wide financing (preferred stock, notes, an ATM program). It does not measure the cost to finish Abilene.

Law-firm release (May 2025): a $15B developer joint venture for the Abilene campus, funded by construction loans. That casts doubt on the scale of the gap, but it leaves out equipment and does not reconcile Oracle's remaining gap.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no reconciled budget for finishing Abilene and no account of Oracle's committed capital. Oracle's corporate financing and the $15B developer package measure different things. Neither shows whether Oracle needed $150B more or less.

semantics.note: "As a result" makes this a causal claim. The universal "every single" scope and the past-tense "subsidized" are kept. It is sweeping but checkable.

contract.note: Reading "losing money" as service-level losses from compute is a plausible ordinary reading given the context. But a net-loss or cash-burn reading would grade the same evidence differently, so the speaker's unstated measure decides the result.

evidence.note: News report: OpenAI's company-wide cash burn in Q1 2026. It does not isolate subscription compute economics or show the claimed cause.

Replit's CEO says the company has been gross-margin positive for over a year. That weighs against universal below-cost provision, but it is unaudited company-wide self-disclosure, not an independent service-level finding.

reviews.rationale: No service-level accounts show every service subsidizing compute and losing money as a result. OpenAI's burn does not establish the cause. Replit's self-reported positive gross margin is a possible counterexample, but it is unverified and fits only one reading of "losing money", so the claim is not settled.

contract.note: Reading "dies" as insolvency or cessation of business is the ordinary meaning of this figure of speech. Requiring documented OpenAI nonpayment before scoring is fair.

evidence.note: Oracle's own release (Oct 27, 2026) announcing expanded OpenAI collaboration. It shows the relationship continuing but proves nothing about payment.
News report: Oracle's force-majeure notice over construction delays at a New Mexico Stargate site. It is not evidence that OpenAI cannot pay.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows no documented OpenAI inability to pay, so the antecedent has not occurred and the conditional is not scored. There is no deadline, and neither a collapse nor a permanent resolution has happened. The forecast remains open.
